_comment: Explicit exceptions to the local clock-gating rules (tools/check-cg.py, docs/rtl-coding-style.md 'Local clock gating'). One entry per module, rule (CG-1, CG-2 or CG-3) and register; why says what was measured and why the rule cannot or should not be met. A waiver that excuses nothing is refused.

waivers.why: A repeater stage exists because its input arrives after a cycle of wire. Any enable that could tell a new valid from a held one has to see that input, and an ICG enable must set up before the flop's own D does, so it would turn a wire-limited path into a gate-limited one. The pulse flops are 3 * SLOTS + 1 a stage; the payload, most of the flops, is gated by this flop (pay_en, 0.0 NGD, DCGE 99-100%). Interim: once a block has RTL, its 2% budget takes these and this waiver is refused as stale.
As valid_q: the credit arrives over the link's wire, so an enable that sees it reaches the clock gate late.
As valid_q: the stall arrives over the link's wire, so an enable that sees it reaches the clock gate late.
As valid_q: the wake arrives over the link's wire, so an enable that sees it reaches the clock gate late. One flop a stage.

The registered wake is the one path from another block into the gate, and Q-49 ends it at a flop so it never reaches a clock gate's enable. An enable that saw `wake` would put it back there. One flop.

6 flops on their own change-only enable (DCGE 100%), under CCV_CG_MIN_FLOPS, so no clock gate. The gate's counters and hold are 14 flops in all, on the free-running clock. One gate over all three needs an enable that ORs the three, past 8 NGD because of the hysteresis compare, or a coarser enable whose DCGE falls to about 0% in idle. Interim: once a block has RTL, its 2% budget takes these 14 flops (CCV_CG_BUDGET_PCT) and this waiver is refused as stale.
